questions.question: The cost price of 42 articles is equal to the selling price of 36 articles. What is the gain or loss made in the transaction?

Gain = SP - CP

Gain% = (Gain)/(CP) x 100

CP = Cost price

SP = Selling price

questions.question: Two trains 400 m and 350 m long are running on the parallel track at the rate of 80 kmph and 90 kmph respectively. If they are running in the same direction, how much time they will take to cross each other?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

(i) Length of train L1 = 400 m & L2 = 350 m

(ii) Speed of Train S1= 80 kmph S2 = 90 kmph

**CONCEPT:**

(i) Relative speed of two train in same direction

**FORMULA USED:**

(i) Relative speed of two train in same direction = S1 – S2

(ii) Relative speed of two train in opposite direction = S1 + S2

(iii) To convert km/hr to m/s = X km/hr = X × ( 5 ÷ 18 ) m/s

**CALCULATIONS:**

Relative speed of two train in same direction = S1 – S2

⇒ (90 – 80) = 10 km/hr = 10 × (5 ÷ 18)

⇒ (50 ÷ 18) m/s

Let, find the total distance covered

⇒ Total distance = sum of length of two train = 750 m

Now, find time taken to cross each other = (distance ÷ speed)

⇒ Time taken = 750 ÷ (50 ÷ 18)

⇒ Time = 750 × (18 ÷ 50)

∴ Time = 270 sec

**∴ Hence, 270 sec. time will be required to cross each other.**

Sublimation: 

__
 
• It is the process in which there is a change of state directly from solid to a gas without changing into a liquid state.

• When ammonium chloride is heated, it gets converted into ammonia and hydrochloric acid.
 
• Common salt (also known as sodium chloride), on the other hand, does not undergo sublimation. 
 
 

Condensation: 

__
 
• The process by which water vapour in the air is changed into liquid water is called condensation. 

 
 
• This caused the water vapour to condense, or turn into its liquid form.
 
• Condensation is crucial to the water cycle because it is responsible for the formation of clouds.
 
 

Evaporation: 

 
• The vaporization occurring from the free surface of a liquid is called evaporation.

 
 
• Evaporation is the escape of molecules from the surface of a liquid.
 
• This process takes place at all temperatures and increases with the increase of temperature.
 
• Evaporation leads to cooling because the faster molecules escape and, therefore, the average kinetic energy of the molecules of the liquid (and hence the temperature) decreases.
 
 

Explanation__:

__
 
• From the above, it is clear that **the transference of molecules from the vapour phase to the liquid phase is called is known as condensation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Boiling: 

 
• As the temperature of a liquid is increased, the rate of evaporation also increases.

 
 
• A stage is reached when bubbles of vapour start forming in the body of the liquid which rises to the surface and escapes.
 
• A liquid boils at a temperature at which the Saturated Vapour Pressure (S.V.P.) is equal to the external pressure.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a principle plane of projection?
questions.solution:
Principal planes of projection are three planes of projection from which the six principal plan views are derived.

**Auxiliary plane is not a principal plane of projection.**

__Different types of planes are:__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/46ad23c571c9387f61bd3c3fd9e3efeb7608effcb84bc6c04e6a58e0f5975588.png] 

1. Reference plane: In general, two planes are employed for projection and are known as reference planes or principal planes of projection. These planes intersect at a right angle to each other.

2. Vertical plane (V.P.): The plane which is vertical is called the vertical plane and is denoted by V.P. Vertical plane is also known as the frontal plane since the front view is projected on this plane.

3. Horizontal plane (H.P.): The plane which is horizontal but at a right angle to the VP. is called the horizontal plane.

4. Auxiliary plane (A.P.): Any other plane, placed at any angles to the principal planes, is called the auxiliary plane.

5. Profile plane (P.P.): The plane which is at right angles to the two principal planes is called auxiliary vertical plane (A.V.P.) or profile plane (P.P.).

6. Reference line: The line of intersection between the principal planes is known as the reference line. It is also called an XY line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bad5af245b2ab3b90624f970690a3206aba9fe67204afb445a629f433dc1bb92.png]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0abfb13e8095a3f5bd5408a71f8e524ef4b4678bf7d032c60473acf841154810.png] 

1. The front view is the view of the object obtained on the V.P. by drawing projectors perpendicular to V.P. from the various corners of the object.

2. The top view is the view of the object obtained on the H.P. by drawing projectors perpendicular to H.P. from the various corners of the object.

3. The side view is the view of the object obtained on the P.P. by drawing projectors perpendicular to P.P. from the various corners of the object.

questions.question: When upper deviation is +0.15 mm and lower deviation is -0.05 mm, than the tolerance on the part is ___
questions.solution:
__Concept:__ 

Tolerance:

__
 
• It is the difference between the maximum limit of size and the minimum limit of size.
 
• **Or It is the difference between the upper deviation and the lower deviation.**
 
• It is always positive and is expressed only as a number without a sign.
 
• So, the tolerance of a hole is the difference between the maximum diameter of the hole and the minimum diameter of the hole.
 
• Similarly, the tolerance of a shaft is the difference between the maximum diameter of the shaft and the minimum diameter of the shaft.

**Upper deviation:**

 
• It is the difference between the maximum size limit and the basic size.

**Lower deviation:**

 
• Lower deviation is the difference between the minimum limit of size and the basic size.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fca8eebc1cdc28d2b0c21c6f44b8fee8ecf01ccee7ebc48b42dac6169675c193.png] 

Basic size:

 
• It is the size based on which the dimensional deviations are given.

Actual size:

 
• It is the size of the component by actual measurement after it is manufactured.
 
• It should lie between the two limits of size if the component is to be accepted.

Limits of size:

 
• These are the extremely permissible sizes within which the operator is expected to make the component.

Maximum limit of size:

 
• It is the greater of the two limit sizes.

Minimum limit of size:

 
• It is the smaller of the two limits of size.

Calculation:__

__Given:__

upper deviation = +0.15 mm and lower deviation = -0.05 mm

Tolerance = (upper deviation) - (lower deviation)

**⇒ Tolerance = +0.15 - (-0.05) = 0.20 mm**

questions.question: Wire can be drawn from metal due to the property called
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Mechanical properties:**

The mechanical properties of a metal are:

 
• ductility
 
• malleability
 
• hardness
 
• brittleness
 
• toughness
 
• tenacity
 
• elasticity

**Ductility:**

 
• A metal is said to be ductile when it may be drawn out in tension without rupture. **Wire drawing depends upon ductility for its successful operation.** A ductile metal must be both strong and plastic. Copper and aluminum are good examples of ductile metals.

**Malleability:**

 
• Malleability is the property of permanently extending in all directions without rupture by hammering, rolling, etc. to change its size and shape. Lead is a very malleable metal.

**Hardness:**

 
• Hardness is a measure of a metal's ability to withstand scratching, wear, abrasion, and penetration.

**Brittleness:**

 
• Brittleness is the property of a metal that permits no permanent distortion before breaking. Cast iron is an example of a brittle metal, and it will break rather than bend under shock or impact.

**Toughness:**

 
• Toughness is the property of a metal to withstand shock or impact. Toughness is the property opposite of brittleness. Wrought iron is an example of tough metal.

**Tenacity:**

 
• Tenacity of a metal is its ability to resist the effect of tensile forces without rupture. Mild steel, wrought iron, and copper are examples of tenacious metals.

**Elasticity:**

 
• Elasticity of a metal is its power of returning to its original shape after the applied force is released. A properly heat-treated spring is a good example of elasticity.

questions.question: Direction of predominant surface pattern is called
questions.solution:
Surface finish, also known as surface texture or surface topography, is the nature of a surface as defined by the characteristics such as lay, surface roughness and waviness.

**Profile:** It is the contour of any specified section through a surface.

**Roughness:** It is defined as closely spaced, irregular deviations on a scale smaller than that of waviness. Roughness may be superimposed on waviness.

**Waviness: **It refers to those surface irregularities that have a greater spacing than that of roughness width. It determined by the height of the waviness and its width. The greater the width, the smoother is the surface and thus is more desirable.

**Lay direction** is the direction of the predominant surface pattern produced on the workpiece by the tool marks.

**Flaws,** or defects, are random irregularities, such as scratches, cracks, holes, depressions, seams, tears or inclusions.
